title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — did they sin vere or falso? False sin cannot be damned by a just judge
pass_a_gloss: He presses the dilemma under Garrigues's own equation: those who earned just condemnation—did they sin truly or falsely? No one will say falsely, because a just judge cannot damn for a falsely alleged sin.
pass_b_english: I ask, then: those who have so sinned that they have earned a just and proper condemnation—have they sinned truly, or falsely? Falsely, I suppose, no one will say. For if someone is said to have so sinned that he has merited just condemnation, and yet one can prove that this is said falsely, it cannot be that he is damned by a just judge for a sin of that kind.
source_text: Quaero igitur, qui ita peccaverunt ut iustam & propriam condemnationem sint commeriti, verumne vere, an falso peccaverint? Falso, opinor, nemo dixerit. Qui enim dicitur ita peccasse ut iustam condemnationem sit promeritus, si potest probare id falso dici, fieri non potest ut ob eiusmodi peccatum damnetur ab iudice iusto.

choices.choice: False sin cannot ground just damnation
